name: prisma
description: Prisma Client 7.10.1 with the TypeScript query compiler and @prisma/adapter-pg, through prisma.$transaction() on a pg.Pool.

modes.description: PrismaClient with a PrismaPg adapter around a pg.Pool. The pool max is the case's pool_max. Interactive transactions use prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => ...), and a nested tx.$transaction() where the case asks for a nested scope. Isolation is the documented isolationLevel option. Prisma's default interactive-transaction timeout (5000 ms) and maxWait (2000 ms) are left in place. No command-tag check, no connection discard, and no extra rollback.

TX-04.independent-inner.reason: Prisma has no propagation mode that promises an independent transaction. A nested tx.$transaction() is a savepoint on the open transaction (SAVEPOINT prisma_sp_N in @prisma/adapter-pg). $executeRaw sends the write when it is awaited, so there are no deferred outer writes for an inner transaction to commit. A separate prisma.$transaction() on the root client is another pooled connection and shares no pending writes with the outer one. The hazard TX-04.3 targets cannot arise.

TX-05.explicit-serializable.reason: Prisma Client 7.10.1's documented transaction API is prisma.$transaction(callback, options) or prisma.$transaction([queries]). Neither returns a handle the application commits with a separate call. The callback form commits when the callback returns. The array form runs the queries and commits inside the one call. Sending BEGIN and COMMIT through $executeRaw would bypass $transaction, so it is not that API.

MG-03.valid-reversal.reason: Prisma Migrate 7.10.1 reads migration.sql and migration_lock.toml. migrate deploy applies that forward SQL and records _prisma_migrations. A migration directory has no down file, and deploy does not run a reversal. This adapter does not add one.
